2026 Long Point Bay Fall Pike Tournament - UPDATE  
 Well we are about a month out from our inaugural fall pike tournament. We have a small update. We have introduced a weather date for this event. If the Saturday weather does not cooperate with us we will be hosting it on Sunday September 27, 2026. That decision will be based on weather forecasts on Friday September 25, 2026. The final decision for a weather change will take place at 4:00pm Friday September 25, 2026. Hopefully we do not need to use it but we want to keep all participants from going out in unsafe conditions. Outside of that, all other details are the same. Please cruise thru the rules and boundaries that were posted on the Facebook page May 29th and if you have any questions feel free to reach out to us at (519)428-4427 or [jesse@jandjaluminum.ca](mailto:jesse@jandjaluminum.ca). Thanks

2026 Long Point Bay Fall Pike Tournament.  
 Things are a go for this Saturday. As of 9am this morning, the weather looks ok but we will continue to monitor that as this week goes on. As for the Duck opener, we are aware of this and ask that anyone looking to fish with us please keep in mind there will be hunters out there. We will look at a possible change in date for next Fall if the numbers attending this event are healthy and will be moving forward in 2027. We will have the tent set up on the wharf out by the Tipsy Pirate Restaurant for registration the morning of. Unfortunately, we will not have the use of the Live Release Boat this weekend. We will look forward to having it back for the Spring Tournament again in 2027. All the tournament details are posted on the Facebook page back on May 29. Please scroll back and look at them, and if you have any questions you can reach out to me at (519) 428-4427 or [jesse@jandjaluminum.ca](mailto:jesse@jandjaluminum.ca).  
 Thanks and see you all on Saturday morning.

2026 Long Point Bay Fall Pike Tournament - CANCELLATION. Erie Bassmasters &[The Long Point Bay Anglers' Association](https://www.facebook.com/LPBAnglers?__cft__[0]=AZhXmw7sFxTMw_n-FsGlvWi5bMU3e3uucNn5nx2KgvQAHE7_HfVs_p4bZXtZUhz8bk3G4NBP1kwMrQoHp9R_CXKPaokaFEBzM7lk2TupD3Of6HxnykIVlIjgxqOdckL7xxbAa3I1Ku5J&__tn__=-]K-R) have made the tough decision to cancel this Saturday's event due to a strong weather event. Several days of strong Easterly winds have caused very poor lake conditions in both the inner and outer bay. Very dirty water, large waves and continuing strong Easterly winds forecasted for both tomorrow and Friday along with strong North East & North winds for Saturday & Sunday have forced us to make this tough decision. We want to get this info out this evening to stay well ahead of the event so all anglers that planned to attend will be aware. We apologize for this decision but conditions are poor and safety is the most important thing to remember. If you know someone planning to attend please reach out to them and pass this info on. We are not re scheduling this event at this time. This is a full cancellation for 2026. We will circle around and look into possibly hosting this event again in 2027 with a possible change in date away from the duck opener. We hope everyone has a great off season and we look forward to seeing everyone at the 2027 Long Point Bay Spring Pike Tournament!!

Title: Fishing Report - Another kick at the walleye and those dam house flies

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/another-kick-at-the-walleye-and-those-dam-house-flies.97901/

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/another-kick-at-the-walleye-and-those-dam-house-flies.97901/post-341889)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/another-kick-at-the-walleye-and-those-dam-house-flies.97901/post-341889)

We decided it was a nice morning and hardly any wind that we best make another cruise to the honey hole.   
 It didn’t disappoint us, started as usual 37-38’ and managed to get all 4 dipsy’s out. My screen showed a lot of hooks. Then all hell broke lose and couldn’t keep the 🤬 farm animals off🤬  
 Got to 42’ and it’s game on, both walleye and house flies. We said enough of this sh$$ when the flies were biting faster than walleye. Even the horse fly spray didn’t stop them from chewing our ankles and feet. Got to 48’ pulled everything and never put tackle away.   
 Came in with 7 and no photo op taken.

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/another-kick-at-the-walleye-and-those-dam-house-flies.97901/post-341892)

*   [#2](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/another-kick-at-the-walleye-and-those-dam-house-flies.97901/post-341892)

I got into the drum as well. Three in a row that were at least 26" long, the biggest being 15lb plus. Had to slow down to 1mph to bring them in from 150ft in less time.

Walleye have moved for sure. Where the screen was full last Thursday it was blank today. I was out from 6:00 till 14:30, found some live water and managed to get 30 or so, but it was not like last week.

The flies were nuts. I suffer the heat with long pants and socks, so the bites were few. I also have several fly swatters on the boat and killed several hundred.

It's amazing the difference a few miles can make... We were out closer to Nanticoke shoal yesterday morning and were amazed at how few bugs there were with the light winds. Not only did the bugs behave but the junk fish stayed away too and we got our three-man limit of nice walleyes very quickly without interference from sheep heads. Fish I have been chasing are still in roughly the same area south of the shoal in 40 to 50 ft of water and haven't really moved for 3 weeks. We never got six rods in the water at all but 7,8 leadcores and a single dipsy all produced well with whatever bait you sent out.

Please keep the bugs and junk fish over at your honey hole Jim, they aren't needed over at ours!

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/any-eyes-on-erieau-today.97950/post-342293)

Thinking Yak Attack BUT....

Frigging wind/weather changes so fast. Saturday WAS looking good....now, blown! Today/this afternoon, according to Windy.com...looks ok. I bit windy now, but calming through morning and shifting more south.

Does anybody have eyes on the lake and thoughts for this aft/eve?

King Joe, hopefully, Outa Here!

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/any-eyes-on-erieau-today.97950/post-342346)

*   [#3](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/any-eyes-on-erieau-today.97950/post-342346)

So, if Windy was a person...I'd hunt that dirty dog down and punch 'em in the nose (a few times).

DID 'trust' Windy and headed for an afternoon/evening run. Driving into Erieau, the speed and the facing direction of the wind turbines already 'hinted' Windy sucks ass. Get to launch about 2:30...when wind was supposed to be calmest of the day....and its basically roaring in my ears....from the south. Lake surface actually looks good....bumpy but no whitecaps. I decide to head out.

Its a strong south wind...and getting stronger as I push through. Closer to shore, maybe 1 in 10 waves break over bow. Almost even with point...1 in 3 over the bow...and the odd, over my legs. BUT, i wanna fish and I am stupid stubborn. I keep pushing out. It takes me an hour to get to 32'...I want to set lines at about 40. Its not getting better, and...yes, Windy sucks bananas....but it did say...WORSENING through afternoon.

At 32'....only....I turn home. FK!

I did head down to Glasgow also....took a look. Was not smooth there either...though the boats out seemed closer than at Erieau (you could not see a boat though lots were out).

On a good note....as I didn't set lines...I am still NOT skunked for this season. Hate Windy.

King Dejected, Outa Here!

Bell declares that Long Point Ontario is actually part of USA

My Bell cell phone charges including “ROAMING in USA” $13 x7 $91.

Any suggestions other than pay up! Thx!

I ran into it several times there with Koodo where it is now $16 a day.   
 Every time they would reimburse it on the next bill or remove it from a future bil after I call them. They were very reluctant to remove that roam like home US service even though I did not ask to activate it initially, but i finally managed to have it cancelled (it is the only service that can not be removed through self-serve). Now I have data roaming disabled and if I see a text from Koodo you re roaming, I m just swirching to an airplane mode while Im there and then reboot the phone at port Rowan. Seems to work so far.

What a coincident, I was billed roaming also after many years with Tellus  
 I have my roaming turned off and finally they sent me charges. I called and explained to them where I was fishing in Canadian waters. Told them also if I cross over the border to fish that I must obtain a State fishing licence. Also told them the border crossing on the lake is far from where I fish in Ontario.   
 All charges were dropped.

Headed down normal time, had to let ourselves in for the boat.

Pretty quiet morning,. possibly five boats seen on the water heading out.

Had a look at 30, then 35, 40, 45, 50 figured better set up or we'll end up state side.

Around 55 things started to show up on the screen so turned left and slowed the descent. 🤨

A few smacks but no hookup so it wasn't all that promising at first.

At 56-57 some hooks and bait combined with the boat's presentation to put one, then another and another and so on into the net.

Nineteen in total made it to the net, nothing lost, no undesirables, no bows. No monsters, all the fish kept are nice eaters.

It was windy, rough with white caps and our quilted shirts stayed on till well into our day.

Water was just under 73* , ran closer to 2.0 today which was much more productive than 2.4 and above. 🤔

Another great trip out on Erie. 🌻

good that you stuck it out. I have noticed on my last 2 trips that the fish were getting lazy. Did better 1.8-2.0 mph than 2.2-2.7mph.

*   [](javascript:)
*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/burwell-9-17-26.98038/post-342967)

If you are no longer fishing Burwell, why not?  
  

[![Image 4: 9133.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72657-d73e3fcacdad93dc6643a634df25b131.jpg?hash=xEUi7JCcEc)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/9133-webp.127102/)
[![Image 5: 9129.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72658-d4a16f2097be7586c998f3c20964a0a8.jpg?hash=7r472BDi0p)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/9129-webp.127103/)[![Image 6: 9128.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72659-21dc411ae2930da09342d8bb84ff59a2.jpg?hash=OOLV7ei00E)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/9128-webp.127104/)

  
 This time fished shallow, it was just as productive as the last trip in 56. (Maybe better)  
  
 East of the river, never went past 50 ft, fish marked from 35 ft on, best for the boat was 46-49ft.  
  
 There were two flags seen today, one in 42 the other further east at 48 ft. Never went past (further east of) the 48 flag, didn't notice the 42 flag until near the end of the trip when heading straight shallow.  
  
 About twenty to the boat, 3 or 4 smalls released to get bigger, another few eaters got lucky and were also let go.  
  
 One impressive strike which morphed into a 💩 head before appearing at the back of the boat was let go without entering the premises. 🤮  
  
 Skitters were terrible at the dock, a few too many flies on the water. Was strange as the breeze should have been enough, maybe due to the distance from shore.  
  
 Water was just under 72*, speed was varied, the usuals did the damage. Minis and a worm harness. 😁🌻

Not sittin on a pier they're not. But as I've said before, fish do NOT know points of the compass. I've had some of my best days off the pier on an east wind. I've had some really good days off the pier with a North wind. When I've been able to get out with someone in their boat, wind direction REALLY didn't matter in terms of catching or not catching. Where wind mattered wasn't the direction it was blowing out of but moreso how hard. Remember, I've been out with [@tailfeathers](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/3405/) when the lake has been "a little bit bumpy" when others wouldn't even dream of going out.

"A little bit bumpy" means, 5-6 ft waves or bigger and we've caught fish. The last several times I've gotten out with him though, it's been a nice boat ride where I didn't really need my sea legs as the lake wasn't all that bumpy.😉

Only if you don't understand that with a north wind, the further out you go, once you're beyond that invisible line that marks where the "protection" the bluffs provide disappears, the bumpier it's likely to get. Also helps to know how to read the lake from shore. With an offshore wind, (winds out of the north) when you're looking south, in close will look almost if not glass flat, but look to where the sky meets the lake, if that 'horizon' appears to have 'bumps', well, those 'bumps' you're seeing, are the tops of the waves and the closer they are to each other, the 'bumpier' it is out there.

 Picked up a few more here and there from 55' to 51'. By then waves were 3'+ so we continued north.  
 Can't say anything was awesome, mad clown, silver/black RRF, banana split and others all pitched in.  
 Dipsey didn't get a sniff all day, 2 on lead and the rest of our 9 all on the riggers.  
 Finished our tour in 40-30' and felt snubbed when the screen was constantly loaded with fish 🤬

title: Early morning smack down outta bruce..
markdown:
Title: Early morning smack down  outta bruce..

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/early-morning-smack-down-outta-bruce.97924/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/early-morning-smack-down-outta-bruce.97924/

Markdown Content:
*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/early-morning-smack-down-outta-bruce.97924/post-342015)

Hit the rich waters of erie with Hawkeye just as the sun was comming up best part of the day !!.Started in 51 ft hit 60 ft needed 2 more soo turned around headed for port and done ..jumped in for a swim with dad ..and high tailed back too port in calm waters ..Bald eagle followed us up the creek made me realize dads looking after us after he passed last September!!

Last weather report I got said rain and thunder storm starting around 10 am at Glasgow so I headed down at 4:00 am. I launched the Legend at 5:00 AM and headed out slowly to 55 fow. 2 dipsy rods at 120 feet back on 3 with black and gold and a yellow and white rrf at 2.7 mph at the ball. All done at 7:25 AM and headed in at 35 MPH because I did not want to get wet if it started early and the lake was almost flat.

Well because of the weather I decided to make a solo trip this morning. Radar showed rain until sunrise so I drove down from London at 4:00 AM and gassed up the Legend. I launched it in the rain at 5:00 AM and went and sat under the south west Gazebo and just enjoyed the morning. The rain did stop just before sunrise so I jumped in the boat and headed out. It was a bit lumpy to start so I decided to stay close to shore and put my first line down in 32' of water at 6:30 AM. Before I could get the other dipsy down the first one went off. I caught 9 fish before I hit 46 fow and tossed back 3 and then headed for shore at 7:10 AM. Cleaning station was good when I got there and good when I left. All 6 fish were spoken for and when I got back to London I zippered and bagged them up. Shown is the weapons of choice this morning.

Markdown Content:
[![Image 1: scrimmy](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/1/1655.jpg?1709653320)](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/scrimmy.1655/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-am-08-26-2026.97941/post-342182)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-am-08-26-2026.97941/post-342182)

Headed to the lake at 4:00 AM because I could not sleep. Put some gas in the Legend then headed to the ramp. I could hear the waves and they were loud. I launched the boat just in case and waited for Brett and Holden to show up at 6:00 AM. I told them it was windy and would be a bit sporty out in the lake so I left the decision up to them. They both decided to give it a go so we headed out to 47 fow to start. Took 45 minutes to get out there. 2 riggers and 2 dipsy rods and no planers put out as it was too rough. It did not take Holden very long until he felt the rath of mother Erie but he hung in there. A bit later Brett was getting the same feeling. It was getting sportier by the minute and they both wanted to call it a day. It took over an hour to slowly make our way back in and it was a bit of a challenge to get back in the channell. I cleaned the 7 fish for them and then put the Legend away and headed home.

title: Glasgow Fri Sept 11 and lost a downrigger ball.
markdown:
Title: Glasgow Fri Sept 11 and lost a downrigger ball.

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-fri-sept-11-and-lost-a-downrigger-ball.98020/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-fri-sept-11-and-lost-a-downrigger-ball.98020/

Markdown Content:
*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-fri-sept-11-and-lost-a-downrigger-ball.98020/post-342877)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-fri-sept-11-and-lost-a-downrigger-ball.98020/post-342877)

With great anticipation took my buddy from orangeville and his 9yr old son out. They've never really fished before so my mind was preoccupied with their having a good time and keeping them safe. I'm setting up my downrigger and put the ball down on the trailer step and forgot about it. Guess it fell off when I was launching. I feel a little stupid 😞. Launch ticket said 11:55am. If anyone reading this happened to come upon a down rigger ball around the east boat ramp, I'd really appreciate it if u can message me. Oh, and it was painted black.

We still had a very good time though, albeit without the use of the downrigger. Boated out to 68' and made use of the SE breeze trolling back with the electric. Love that auto pilot. Speed was 1.3mph to 2.0mph. Most hook ups 1.3 - 1.5. 3 rods in hand, 2 of which weighted with inline sinkers and homemade spinners tipped with worms and the 3rd with a weight forward spinner. Had a fourth setup using a 4oz inline sinker dragging a jointed J11.

Actually didn't take long to get the first hit - my line lol. I handed the rod to buddy's kid who fought it for a bit and the fish spit it. Too bad cuz it felt like a good one. A while later got another hit and handed to the kid again. Meanwhile my buddy got one on - "double header". Both lost. 😞 I was shaking my head on the inside. Lol. What we should have done was circle back and work that area.

Most of the action we had was at 65' - 60' and in the 40's. Final tally, 8 keepers including a 17" that we kept cuz it was the kids first walleye. We also got a 26" and a 26-1/2. The hot blade colours were black with orange strip and black with chartreuse strip counting for 5 in the boat. Haven't used these colours here except [@SkinnyTiller](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/10003/) reported he was catching using fire tiger pattern. The grey/black J11 accounted for 1 fish. We lost 6 hook ups. The fish were very spunky.

The activity on the sonar was predominantly at 40' and above. Hooks between 20' and 40' and the bait balls above that. At one point it looked like the appearance of a thermocline at 35' when we were trolling in the 50' depths but it eventually disappeared.

Everyone had a great time. I think they got the bug now. And drop me a message if you found a downrigger ball.

Started in 47 fow with 2 dipsies and 2 riggers. Only used the 4 rods as I did not put out the big Planer boards. Just as well as I could only keep up with the 4 rods. Same program I have been running for the last few weeks. If it is not broke why change. We ended before 10 AM with 20 fish brought into the boat and 2 returned. Waited a bit at the cleaning station to clean the 18. Left it in good working condition after unplugging it a couple times. Unlike Luke's dad Mike who lost fish last week Luke never lost a one and I made him reel in most as he has never caught a Walleye before. I told him to rub it in to his dad. After cleaning fish I dropped off some to Greg and then to George on my way back to London.

Headed out this afternoon  
 Started in 45fow picked them off steady out to 66fow  
 Lots of action on the sonar  
 85-130 on dipsy 3 settings caught fish  
 Riggers down 40-50 and slider also caught fish  
  
 Lost a few really big ones due to their thrashing once in the prop wash.  
  
 For the most part surface was 76ish and down 45 was 60-66  
 Did run threw a patch of 76 surface 74 all the way down at 50ft quickly turned away from that

> Made it down after work launched around 3:45pm with Slancy and Brad   
>  Hog city  
>  Tossed back a couple smalls   
>  Fish was hungry 60-68fow   
>  Dipsys 85-95 on 3   
>  75 on 1.5   
>  And riggers deep hitting sliders 45-55ft   
>  They lovin the ripplins and lil whackers today   
>  Wonderbread lil whacker did a lot of damage   
>  Purple rrf and nascar rrrf caught some too

Tried for Saturday but weather not much better than Friday. Launched and slowly headed out in rough seas. Put 2 dipsy rods out in 32 fow and trolled out to 62 fow with the waves building and the wind picking up as well. Marked a total of 3 fish from 32 to 62 fow without a touch. Waves were building so I did the smart thing and pulled the rods and headed for shore. There were a few boats out there but not sure if they faired any better than I did. I will wait for a calm day and if not I will put the Legend away for the winter.

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-sept-4th-evening-hunt.97980/post-342566)

Well the stars finally aligned and got out for my next therapy session   
 We were looking at the forecast all week saying maybe tomorrow evening. 🤷🏻   
 Met up with [@SkinnyTiller](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/10003/) in Glasgow around 3:30ish   
 Made the trek out to the fishing grounds got mostly set up before getting the first fish in the box. I don’t even remember the order we caught so many it wasn’t fast and furious but steady Eddie with the odd lull   
 We got pickier than picky and referred to ourselves as snobs throwing back perfectly good fish. To extend our evening by an hour or so   
 Eventually kept our last few and head in   
 Lake was beautiful storms went away no rain almost sunshining.   
 Lost the big fish of the day 40 ft from the boat.   
 Hi hit the dipsy with a Wally diver. 🤷🏻

Think it was even Steven between the dipsys and riggers

Dipsy 3 setting 110 with lil whackers   
 Riggers at 40-45 with slider   
 But main line with lil whackers caught most   
 Last couple fish came on a green spoon off dipsy.

Forecast changed afternoon looked like it had potential so called in the dream team to give it another hooo raw   
 We also hadn’t been together in Glasgow yet   
 Should be interesting   
 Sure enough this morning I realized I didn’t plug in my trolling motor batteries to charge last night so got it going this morning but by the time I wanted to leave it still didn’t say they were done.. oh well un plugged away I went.   
 Thankfully we had enough juice to finish our trip.   
 Channel was rocking and rolling when I got there oh well launched on the east ramp anyways   
 Was banking on it being better when we got back   
 It wasn’t..   
 it did lay down nicely while we were out but the rollers were still coming in from the south east   
 Set up lines in 67fow and trolled north west with the waves copied last nights program   
 Wonderbread was the ticket so put extra Wonderbread stuff out.   
 A Wonderbread RRF was on its way down to 130ft back but got smacked at 95 while I still had the bail open and thumb on the spool 😂   
 Didn’t take many pics but some nice ones.   
 I think our camera man probably got some and will post later   
 18 in the box   
 Text Slancy on our way in so her Mayday and Madalyn met us for food after.   
 Also met up with our Friend Joy and Dave at the cleaning station. They got into some nice ones as well

Title: Fishing Report - Glasgow September 29th AM

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-september-29th-am.98070/post-343207)

Well I launched the Legend around 6:00 AM and headed straight out to 62 fow. First rod in at 7:00 AM. 1 Dipsy rod back 142 on 3 and 1 rigger down 52'. First fish came in 65 fow off the rigger with pink panties spoon at 2,7 mph. Next fish in 67 fow off the dipsy with RRF. Most fish came in at 65 to 70 fow. Things are slowing down as it took me a couple hours to get my limit of 6. Headed in at 9:00 AM and stopped in 32 fow to clean my 6 then headed for shore. Cleaning station is closed for the season so clean them on the lake or at home. Good luck to anyone still gowing out.

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-wednesday-am-09-16-2026.98030/post-342927)

Well I launched the Legend around 6:00 AM this morning and it did not look too bad out of the channel so away I went. I started to mark lots of fish in 45 fow so I slowed the boat down and setup there and figured I would troll south. Tons of fish down all around 30 feet. Set up 2 dipsy rods with rrf's and back 67 and 65 feet. Had my limit in no time at all. Finished around 8:00 AM and looked for the group from Point Au Baril. Found them and told them how I was catching my fish. They told me they had 1 in the box so I figured they would do OK so I bid them farewell and headed to the cleaning station which was good when I got there and good when I left. I figure yesterdays storm brought the fish alot closer to shore so go out and get you some. I have a bunch of tests to go through at St. Joes on Friday so most likely won't be back out until Monday.

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-with-mike-and-barebones-charters.97926/post-342045)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/glasgow-with-mike-and-barebones-charters.97926/post-342045)

I went out of Pt Glasgow with Mike and Barebones Charters yesterday. Left the dock at 1030, back by 1230.  
 There are no shortage or walleye out there right now..quick limits of quality fish. Ran typical setups with 2 Dipsies straight out the back with metal, deep divers off the sides. Immediate action. The unique part of yesterday was Mike and his charter setup.  
 He runs a 20' Lund Alaskan, with a Merc 150 tiller. Full electronics, great quality equipment, like most charters...but his is different. You're not in a 24, 26, 30' walkaround or cruiser, you're in an open 20' Alaskan. Rather than 4 or 5 other people, it was Mike and me...thats it. Open air, bouncing around a bit, fighting fish. Great conversation, talked about how he got going with this approach which is different. Highly recommended for a real deal day on the water!

Mike commented that when he has 3 or 4 people that don't necessarily know how to help with setting lines, grabbing hits, etc, he spends 99% of his time at the back of the boat anyways. He uses a bow mount electric that tied into his graphs and gps to auto-pilot, using the tiller to power. Its very efficient with setting lines, netting, etc. I always have fun on the big charter boats, even when I ran my own 22' Trophy, but honestly, this was a totally different experience. *   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/lpb-sept-29.98078/post-343239)

Left Port D around 6:00 and headed SE. Stopped in 25fow to have look at the graph and there was lots of life. Debated starting there but figured with calm in the water forecast I would keep going. Stopped at 35fow and then again at 40fow and figured that was far enough. Dropped a couple of glow worm harnesses 75 and 100 ft back behind #1 dipsys around 6:30 and had a limit to the boat by 7:15. Only kept one that was hooked bad.

The plan was to start shallow and head deep to see if I could find some rainbows or cohos. Had the lake pretty much to myself until about 8:00-8:30, then the other boats showed up and by the time I got close to deep water there were too many for me to join the crowd. Too tough to navigate when solo.

Stayed in the 40-50fow range most of the day, switching between longlining cranks and various spoons and RRF behind dispys. Got a rainbow in 43fow on a spoon, then had another follow as I was ripping a spoon back to the boat as fast as I could crank. Saw it at the last second 5 ft behind the boat before it peeled off. Switched to two spoons for a hours with nothing to show.

Back to switching things up between cranks, spoons, worm harnesses, with steady action. Slower, 1.8 - 2.2 mph, seemed to work better again for me. Several double headers including when I was packing up at 2:30. The last hit of the day was another rainbow I think, not sure because I had the other rod in my hand reeling in a walleye. The one in the holder was going nuts but I forgot to lighten the drag when I put the rod back out, so the fish eventually got off.

Not sure how many fish I caught, a bunch. Only kept 2 nice 22-24" walleye and the rainbow. The bow had 3" long shad in its belly. Midges and stable flies were annoying, and the gill netters are back in the bay. Saw a line of nets between the elbow and the point, likely along the 70-80 ft contour. I did not get close enough to see if there were any jugs, just saw a couple of end flags and the boat.

One of these days I will figure out how to take selfies and post some "action shots".

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/lpb-tuesday-night-bass-series-season-wrap-up.97965/post-342450)

SEASON WRAP UP. I just wanted to jump on this morning to say thanks to a few people. First off, thanks to everyone that came out this season and joined us for our Tuesday night events. We appreciate you all and can't wait to see you all again next season. Second, huge thanks to Brad Thomson for getting our scales set up, weighing our fish, and taking the scales down. He has been there since the beginning and shows up every Tuesday for us, thanks so much Brad. Finally, thanks to MacDonald Turkey Point Marina for hosting us. We wouldn't be able to do it without you. This season came and went fast with 5 of 9 events planned in, few cancellations but we got an extra one in at the end!! Next seasons schedule will officially come out later this year, but looking at the calendar today it will likely start Tues June 29 and run thru until Tues Aug 31 for a total of 10 events. We are going to run the Long Point Bay Open again next year as well. Next year will be our 4th season. We enjoy running these events and will continue to bring a fun, competitive weekly tournament to you guys. If anyone has any questions, concerns or ideas for these event going forward, feel free to reach out to me [jesse@jandjaluminum.ca](mailto:jesse@jandjaluminum.ca) or 519-428-4427.  
 Season Highlights: Biggest 3 LM bag of the season was 11.80 for 3 fish. The biggest LM of the season was a 4.48. The biggest 3 SM bag was 14.72 for 3 fish. The biggest SM of the season was a 5.89.  
 Our plan is to 50/50 the events again next year with LM and SM, with LM being available to weigh in at every event.  
 Thanks again and have a great off season!!

Title: Fishing Report - Monday September 14th at Glasgow

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/

[![Image 1: scrimmy](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/1/1655.jpg?1709653320)](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/scrimmy.1655/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342912)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342912)

Well I met Brad and his crew from Point Au Baril at 6:00 AM on Monday at his 22 foot Stanley. We headed out in some sporty seas out to 55 fow. Brad had only 2 big John Riggers with 2 rod holders on them so we were limited to 4 rods. It was there first trip to Erie and they were eager to learn. We fished the morning then went back for lunch and returned to fish the afternoon until 6:30 PM and headed back to shore. The lake did calm down in the afternoon. I tried to show them what I could with the limited equipment on the boat. Same program I have been running the past few weeks. I hope they enjoyed the trip. I believe we finnished with about 20 fish. No pictures as I was kind of busy. I told them I did not think they would be fishing on Tuesday but I would likely be back Wednesday morning with my boat if the weather co-operated and I would call them on the radio.   
 See less

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342913)

*   [#2](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342913)

Sounds like you gave it the good old college try. Been there as well. It is funny how frustrating it can be when they just don't quite have the right gear. I am sure that they learned a lot though, good on you for the effort.

[![Image 2: scrimmy](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/1/1655.jpg?1709653320)](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/scrimmy.1655/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342917)

*   [#3](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/monday-september-14th-at-glasgow.98026/post-342917)

> Sounds like you gave it the good old college try. Been there as well. It is funny how frustrating it can be when they just don't quite have the right gear. I am sure that they learned a lot though, good on you for the effort.

I did give Brad a list of what to get for his boat like at least 8 cannon rod holders and a proper mast for planer boards amd di[sy rods as well as big planer boards. He did by a half mast which is too small and he bought inline boards thinking they were for the mast. He only had 2 level wind dipsy rods so I brought 2 of mine as well and they caught most of the fish. They are eager to learn and I will likely see them out Wednesday morning and guide them with my radio. They are heading back home Wednesday afternoon. I do however love the 22' Stanley Center Console.

# Nanticoke Labour Day

*   Thread starter[Tacklebuster](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/tacklebuster.8172/)
*   Start date[Sep 9, 2026](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/nanticoke-labour-day.98003/)

[T](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/tacklebuster.8172/)

#### [Tacklebuster](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/tacklebuster.8172/)

##### Well-Known Member

*   [Sep 9, 2026](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/nanticoke-labour-day.98003/post-342724)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/nanticoke-labour-day.98003/post-342724)
*   [](javascript:)
*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/nanticoke-labour-day.98003/post-342724)

I few weeks ago I took out a my future daughter in-law's younger brother and he had a great time. So much so, that his older brother had been asking if we could go on a fishing trip too. So, on Labour day we went. I couldn't think of a better way to spend the last day of your summer break and I am quite sure they agreed. My son also came along, which was great because he's knows the ropes. I told the boys that I was going to show them how to set lines, land fish, safely unhook them, bleed them, and then they would take over and I would mostly drive. I think they loved it, I didn't land one fish and it was a blast watching them.  
  
 First stop was our usual area in 60 FOW, there were a ton of marks, but very much to my surprise for the first hour we barely got a sniff. Multiple phantom hits on the riggers, and the dipseys, but nothing landing in the net. We eventually landed a small 14"er which confirmed what I suspected and we headed for 70-80 FOW. The marks looked better, but we got into an area where the bottom 15' was covered in bait. which I also don't like. Nonetheless, we started picking off a few. The catch rate still seemed slow, so I changed our speed from 2.7-2.9 down to 2.5 and that made all the difference. We started catching as usual, had two tripples which got chaotic, it was hilarious.  
  
 RRF BG worked best on Dipseys, but the riggers also worked. Spoons caught a few.  
  
 When we got back home, I showed the brothers how to fillet, they got right into it.  
  
 Overall, a great trip.

Title: Fishing Report - PORT BRUCE- Better Than Day Before

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/

[![Image 1: SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/post-342828)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/post-342828)

Good turnout at noon, waited for 4 boats to trailer before launching 12:30. Said hi to [@Consequence Free](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/2266/) at the breakwall on his way back in. Near perfect conditions on way out to 58fow again, dropped lines ~1 with couple other boats in general vicinity. Dipsys with Gibbs/HJ14 to start- couple quick hits on the Gibbs before it snagged 1st fish over 59fow. Mixed baits up a little, headed deeper, things got quiet by 62.6fow so turned E for a spell looking to get back on fish. Encouraging outbound leg with 2 fish lost (both off Nascar RRF) but 8 boated with calm conditions holding.

Headed N briefly then W, no action so swapped baits, waited and was back on active fish by 58fow. Quick flurry of 4 fish over 56/55fow then hooked into 4 more with just one rod out by 5pm, last one on P10 over 47fow. 10/10 on the inbound W-N track, brought 4 home. Dipsy leads on 3 were 86-110', on 1 were 83-110' and speeds were 2.3-2.9mph depending on the baits. Good to see so many out today enjoying the stellar weather and fishing.

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/post-342885)

*   [#17](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-better-than-day-before.98014/post-342885)

> Good turnout at noon, waited for 4 boats to trailer before launching 12:30. Said hi to [@Consequence Free](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/2266/) at the breakwall on his way back in. Near perfect conditions on way out to 58fow again, dropped lines ~1 with couple other boats in general vicinity. Dipsys with Gibbs/HJ14 to start- couple quick hits on the Gibbs before it snagged 1st fish over 59fow. Mixed baits up a little, headed deeper, things got quiet by 62.6fow so turned E for a spell looking to get back on fish. Encouraging outbound leg with 2 fish lost (both off Nascar RRF) but 8 boated with calm conditions holding.
> 
> 
> Headed N briefly then W, no action so swapped baits, waited and was back on active fish by 58fow. Quick flurry of 4 fish over 56/55fow then hooked into 4 more with just one rod out by 5pm, last one on P10 over 47fow. 10/10 on the inbound W-N track, brought 4 home. Dipsy leads on 3 were 86-110', on 1 were 83-110' and speeds were 2.3-2.9mph depending on the baits. Good to see so many out today enjoying the stellar weather and fishing.

I recognized you coming in as I was heading out and I yelled hello to you.   
 Thanks for sharing your information with me.  
 I stayed shallow (43 fow) and didn't run out to 57 like you had said only because of the amount of daylight left. I did well using a blue/silver rrf on a #1 dipsey 3 setting 120 back. Caught my limit by 7:30 and back to the docks just before dark.

Good turnout with 13 trailers parked when launching 10:30. Sweet conditions awaited beyond the pier- headed S and set up over 58fow ~11:15- Gibbs and glow RRF off Dipsys. No life on screen or action heading downhill until 62 fow- 1st on Redfin. Rescued a 'Penguin' along my track to 64fow where Gibbs popped off w 2nd. 3rd fish came over 65fow on BBerry Muffin wormburner and was last one until turning W over 67fow, 14 miles out.

Didn't wait long for 4th on Nascar RRF, 5th and 6th on HJ14- Helsinki Shad all off Dipsys 86-110' on 1. Hooked into a double header at the end of my W track- looked up to notice a flag- landed both and turned 180° to avoid the net. Pink Squirrel picked 2 off the rigger ⬇️ 50' and Wonderbread wormburner finished the day at 4:30 with 2 more. Marked bait and fish sporadically from 63-67fow, went 12/13 with speeds 2.3-2.6, target depth 40-50' ⬇️ with 65-67fow producing most fish- just one at 18 1/2"", rest thick 20-24". Great day and conditions to be out fishing deep- burned under 6 gal. in 5 hrs tracking over 32 miles by route 👌

Launched ~2 with only 2 other trucks in the lot. Split the difference in intel- nice fish being caught in 30fow and good fishing beyond 58fow- and paid the price. Setup over 39fow going downhill, water 71°F and chalky until 41fow with wind and chop out of SW. Ran RRFs and spoons off Dipsys for 50 mins to 48fow then swapped in a jointed, floating Rapala ( blue back). Coaxed one on the Rapala over 49.3fow. Switched 2nd rod to Rigger pulling DHJ12s and Bandits w cheater/spoons and trolled out to 53fow then doubled back with wind and building chop at the stern. Picked off just 1 more on the Rapala back over 48fow. Marked small streaks of bait and decent #s of fish in the top 19' from 39 to ~45fow but very little beyond to 53fow. Consolation fish both came on jointed Rapala off Dipsy on 3 w 57' out.

Went out after work today with a buddy. Passed the port bruce lighthouse at 559pm. Motored out to the area I been working for last 3 weeks in 59'. I found an area with alot of current and it has been holding fish. The screen very nice out there, showing alot of marks and bait...... a few times, I told my buddy "look at those marks, we're going to get a bite" . and it happened....Set the first rod out and had a fish on before 2nd rod was in. Fishing was great. Rods in at 8pm. Went 19/22 and 1 farm animal. Rods that was far and above the others was #1 dipsy, 1 setting, out 60' with greasy chicken wing- copper backed. Had 2 other greasy chicken wing with silver back, but copper back out produced everything 2-1. .. on a side note, the weather Bouy was a bit off... It said 0.3 and it was probly more than that in the creek. was a bit sporty on the lake ..but manageable. . Wind kept the flies away anyways. Beautiful evening out there. Was picking away ..hit 54 ft ..big bow hit the slider and wasn't hooked that good bye!!...wind shifted 3 times we were out never seen that in my 40 yrs on erie!!.?Everything that didn't make sense..happened at the end of the day nice 3 hrs with my not soo baby girl!! ..on the way home almost got smoked again wtf ..got home cleaned the 11 we brought home. I remember a couple years ago there were a bunch of dead fish washed up on the beach in Pt. Bruce. Wasn't from cold oxygen starved water, it was from a commercial boat who hadn't punctured their air bladders before throwing the unwanted overboard. Made a couple inquiries this am re: recent fish die-off where lots of drum fell victim. According to MNR this happens regularly and while there can be a few causes the most recent was likely caused by upwelling- persistent strong winds from NW/N/NE that push warmer water out from shore allowing colder, oxygen-depleted water to move shallow/to surface. The possibility for upwelling exists every year but it usually occurs every couple yrs. when prevailing weather creates the conditions for this phenomena where sheephead are most affected.

  
  

### [Canadian Authorities Investigate Mystery Fish Kill in Lake Erie](https://ictnews.org/archive/canadian-authorities-investigate-mystery-fish-kill-in-lake-erie/)

A recent fish kill of tens of thousands of carp, sheepshead, perch, catfish, suckers, big head buffalo and other species on the shores of Lake Erie was caused by a natural temperature inversion that pushed cold water lower and brought oxygen-poor water to where the fish were swimming, killing...

Got down to Bruce and had couple sausage on a bun (w fried onions) waiting for conditions to taper. Getting ready to launch and ended up chatting with 3 lads from Mitchell/Stratford that used the wonderbread tip from yesterday to fill some limits this am 👍👍 Too bad my day-old intel didn't pan out (more to come 😆). Ready to launch and who pulls out but [@Consequence Free](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/2266/) so of course we had to catch up- good to see ya again with fish CF! Finally launched 2:15- conditions still snotty with swell coming up Catfish round last bend.

Info from yesterday was limits and big fish were caught shallow, as in 28fow. Set-up over 29fow with crankbaits and boards and started marking LOTS of bait and fish. Forgot the worms at home 🙄- might have had luck with harnesses and bottom bouncers. Trolled for 1hr 35mins out to 46fow switching cranks then running Dipsys with everything that didn't require worms- lost 1 on blue jointed Rapala (floater). Gave up and went deeper on intel from [@CBS](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/4492/) this am.

Reset over 59fow with wind and waves still out of SE running a Dipsy/P10 and a crankbait off rigger with cheater spoon. 1 fish on P10, 0 on rigger so went RRFs off Dipsys out to 63fow and back into 58 where the pin was pulled at 7pm. Managed just 4/7 all on chartreuse RRF/Firetiger Dipsy on 3 w leads 88-94. Marked and caught fewer fish today but day ended nicely once wind finally died and chop started to settle.

Lone truck in the lot launching 12:30. Word was limits 38-45fow. Slowed over 36fow and set lines after seeing the graph- fish and bait were stacked! Wonderbread and Blueberry Muffin worm burners off Dipsys. 3 cleanouts on Wndrbrd before 1st fish on BBerry Muffin over 38fow. Kept trolling downhill, bumped 53fow and turned back on track, last fish over 40fow. Leads 44-71' on 3 and 60-83' on 1, speeds 2.2-2.6, best results 38-41fow and 48-51. Wormburners did best with P10, Gibbs and Gr. Ch. RRF chipping in- lost 2 beauts but boated 11.

Chewed the fat for a couple and was off to the south setting up over 54fow.

Picked up just 2 by 58fow- wind had picked up and swung around out of the W with chop building. Pulled lines and ran out to 62fow to troll back in, calling it over 51fow ~3 with wind blowing 17mph and waves 2 1/2-3'. Marked both bait and fish but pulled just 4 aboard and losing 2 on the flip- came home with 2. Nothing on riggers w cheater or DHJ12s w 6/8oz.- Redfins saved the day off Dipsys 71-97' out on 3 (Nascar 2/3, Gr. Ch. 1/2 and Duracell 1/1)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-tuesday-august-18th.97911/post-341942)

After fantastic service at NEM we were on Erie by 7am. There was a little walleye chop first thing so by 40 fow we put the brakes on and started with 320’ of 4 colour leadcore dragging a black/gold rrf. Didn’t take long and we managed the biggest fish of the day. Photo opportunity. Got the leadcore back quickly and added a dipsy each side back 75’ & 80’ on #2s. One dipsy with black/gold rrf the other with blue/silver rrf. Trolled out to 59 fow and headed back with zigs zags and few donuts. It took longer to get our limits due to the guy on the net screwing up. Good thing he’s the captain too. I even had one flip out of the boat for a good laugh. After we got our 12 we maintained course and cleaned the fish on the way in. It’s so nice not to deal with the carcasses on land and give the nutrients back to the lake. Only when the lake is flat will I do that. When we got back to NEM we met SkinnyTiller. Nice to meet you SkinnyTiller. I really enjoy your posts. I won’t tell anyone about your secret lures you’ve been saving for 2 years. What a great day on Erie.

Nobody else in the parking lot when launching 12:30. Missed the best part of the 'window' by ~ 1 1/2 hrs with tight chop and wind from NE. Played it safe and started at 1pm over 30fow with harnesses and BBs doing 2.1mph with lots of life on screen- 3 cleanouts, no takers. Switched to Dipsys and wormburners at 2.8mph over 38fow with almost no life on screen now- 2 cleanouts, still no takers by 45fow. Threw RRF out on 1 Dipsy with B Berry wormburner on 2nd Dipsy out to 50fow (doing 2.5 mph) where I doubled back with wind blowing 15+ and tight NE chop building, calling it a day over 46fow- 1 fish caught! Water 70°F and clear with good visibility. Few boats out earlier had good luck out low 60s fow with a few big ones in the mix. Resident Heron posed for a (bad) close-up on the way upstream.

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-where-were-all-the-anglers.98011/post-342800)

Had no intention of fishing today (honestly!) so was enjoying a mid-morning coffee when a text came thru: "if ur fishin today I've got the day off" 🤔 👀 at conditions- wind N 5.8kts waves 3.2' 🤨, by 11 it was game on with wind WSW 1.9kts and 2' waves on 3sec. Stopped for another couple sausage on buns while waiting for [@Tyler0420](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5512/) to arrive in Bruce. Only 3 trucks in the lot when we launched 12:30ish, took a leisurely cruise out to 58fow checking a few depths for life along the way.

Set up w 4 Dipsys and worm-based baits to start ~1:15pm- 86'/102' on 1 and 83'/100' on 3- covering 35-50'. Fish came in fits and spurts with 60/61fow having least amount of action. Didn't mark much on the screen but a few bait and speed changes with longer leads kept the fish coming- speeds 2.3-2.7mph ⬇️ 40-50'. Had couple handfuls hitnruns, lost 5 fish (3 nice ones just beyond the net) and boated 18 out to 63fow with last fish (balloon pic) at 4:30. Despite the overcast moving in from W the wind had died and lake had laid down nicely for the 10 mile cruise back in. Only 1 other trailer in lot when we docked on such a nice afternoon.... oh well, Tyler got his limit.

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-bruce-wormburner-from-lambeth-rod-and-tackle-to-the-rescue.97992/post-342656)

Waited for 6 boats to trailer before launching at 1- chatted with 3 who said they cut things short on account of conditions with no fish... 👌 Channel was sloppy but quite a few folks enjoying the holiday with lines in the water. Headed S to 49fow with 2 1/2' chop and wind out of SE/E. Slow going to start, lost 1 over 55fow then started boating fish over 56fow. Ran 20+ baits off Dipsys and 6 Bandits/Goldminers w 8oz snap out to 62.4fow then back in, finishing up over 56fow ~ 5pm.

Lost 1st fish off Bandit, boated 1st one on Deep Threadfin P10 off Dipsy (84' on 3). Hit a couple slow spells so swapped baits often. Nothing fired until I paired a Wonderbread wormburner from Dreamweaver with Wonderbread Dipsy. Tried bunch of baits on same lead and setting as Wonderbread combo but didn't get a whiff, including Gibbs and 2 RRFs with worms... Gibbs managed 1 fish. Speed was 2.4-2.7mph. Marked little bait and fewer fish but managed 14/15 with ole Wonderbread doing the heavy lifting (12) out 94/97' on 3. Was resetting it at one point with drag loose and caught an 'eye with only 38' line out! Wind finally died down 4ish putting a nice ending to a pretty good day.

> Tell me more about the Smoked Walleye 😁

A quarter cup of salt and water in a zip lock bag! Put the fillet in the bag and in the fridge overnight. In the morning rinse well and dry off. Place on your smoker rack and spread some liquid honey over it dust with black pepper and maybe some garlic powder and smoke using corn cobs to make the smoke. I like mine a little dry but smoked this way you will be amazed.

How long do you recommend

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-burwell-walleye.97892/post-341912)

*   [#16](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-burwell-walleye.97892/post-341912)

> How long do you recommend?

There are so many variables that you cannot name a specific timeframe, but you know you’re there as the surface liquid turns dry and tacky.

With white fish anywhere from 30-120 mins uncovered in the fridge is good enough while fatty fish like salmon I let it go longer to be sure the fats are sealed in.

Do this for meats too, sometimes allowing it to dry overnight in the fridge. Drying in a cool dark place with a fan for circulation is very common too.

Buddy wanted some fish for a fry. Plan was Stanley but I wasn’t like the chances. Set the alarm for 4am, bouy reading at 1.3 and 1.6 at 5. Texted buddy told him our only option was Dover as it’s off shore there but never fished it or reschedule for another day. Dover it was. Left London at 6 on water for 8. Beautiful marina and ramps were top notch. Figured I read enough reports from here that I could figure something out. Headed down the shoreline until I hit stelco Set up in 47fow and trolled around the shoal. Definitely a different experience with the currents and waves. Set up was 3 dipseys, 2 leadcore and flatline. Tried gold miners, bandits and huskyjerks with and without snap weights but couldn’t get a flatline to fire. Swapped it out for another dipsey. Numerous spoons and bodybaits hit the water. Dipseys were top producer. Leadcore both 5 and 4 chipped in. To rough to circle back on fish. Best depth was 80 down 35ish. Will have to give it another go in better conditions to figure out the flatlines. Hit a couple way points for future reference. Only a cooler picture as buddy took home all the fish. Lil whacker on the end took half the fish. The rest contributed.

Went out this morning with [@Mickey Finn](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/4009/) and our grandson. First fish on after only a few minutes, but catching his first fish on lead core with 6 colours out proved to be too much of a challenge. He made up for it by catching his limit on the downriggers! We had just put split rings on my favourite two RAC spoons so we pulled them out of retirement and they were the winners, outfishing the pink panties! 66 FOW, running both riggers down 40 feet. #### [CBS](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/cbs.4492/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-glasgow-aug-29.97959/post-342383)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-glasgow-aug-29.97959/post-342383)

After reading Derek9 and Scrimmy the walleye slayers reports I figured I would give the old stomping grounds a try. Bouy was reading 1 when I left London so I was expecting a bouncy day. Launched at 6:30 to see 4 boats heading back to the ramp with easy 2-4ft waves. Slow ride out to 65fow. Turned and trolled with the waves back to 60. 12 in the cooler and called it a day. No fish released, all lines set down 35. It was nice change from Stanley. Season pass was a great investment and I love the ramp in Stanley minus the walk but 60fow is a long way out. Glasgow is a great marina, had a slip there in 2010. Half the drive to 60 and seems to hold more fish. Maybe it’s just me but the ramp sure has a good lean to it. Need a second person to hold the boat in place when pulling out. Black and white took 3, green with dots took 1, pink took 2 and green,pink,yellow took 6.

Finally got out to Port Maitland for what will most likely be our last trip of the season, and it was a good one.

We worked 90 FOW, targeting 50–70 ft down, and the body baits were absolutely on fire. Dipsy Divers trolled around 2.7 mph produced steady action and kept the rods moving.

We were working on the last walleye for our limit when the last rod suddenly fired. Ended up with a doubleheader to finish the day—the walleye we needed and what looks to be a coho to cap things off.

Couldn’t have asked for a better way to potentially end the season. The cooler was full, the rods were working, and we got off the water with a pretty memorable finish.

Port Maitland — 90 FOW | 50–70 ft down | 2.7 mph | Body baits | Dipsys

If this really was the last trip of the season, I’d say we went out on a high note.

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/port-maitland-took-a-while.98040/post-342984)

Haven't been down to Maitland for almost 2 yrs so figured it's about time, but not without touching base with one of the local 'Sheriffs' first. Arranged to meet up with [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) at FishMasters around noon- outside of roadwork (still) in Delhi, was a nice 2 1/2 hr drive down #3 . After greetings, handshakes and a couple of 6-8 coasters passing hands, we launched and I followed down the Grand and out to open water. Set up over 82fow with Dipsys and RRFs. Managed 2/3 in first 25 mins and got cocky- released both. Trolled 80-90 fow catching 4 more by time [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) and his fishing partner pulled up alongside to have a good chat before they headed in. Stuck it out to 4:30 when the rain started- pulled the pin having hooked 3 more. Dipsy leads on 1 were 86-130' (most fish at 102'), speeds 2.2- 2.9 (last 3 fish at higher speeds). Wonderbread glow RRF got 1st, Nascar RRF went 1/2 losing a goodun but caught 2 in 4th qrtr and wormburners (wonderbread & blueberry muffin) did the rest. Have found Maitland a tough nut to crack with big range of depths and the fish can be anywhere in the column. Big thanks to [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) for the introduction to FishMasters (1st time)👍👍, providing the need-to-know and the guided escort 🍻👊 Took a while but 10th trip was a charm- 9 fish and great conditions... best yet!

Hey [@SkinnyTiller](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/10003/), how did you like the missile launcher...I mean boat ramp? I used to live just down the road overlooking Mohawk Island, but only launched at Fishmasters 1X. Great place, nice setup for mooring, but the ramp is out of this world, at least used to be. It was so steep that the door of the truck would not stay open I had fight my way out of the truck. Had a bugger of time getting the boat back on the trailer correctly as well.

It is a nice area to fish, lots of bottom contour and deep and shallow shoals. You can catch a limit in 100fow or 20fow if you want. I liked it for that reason, it allows me to expand my bag of tricks. If the wind is bad from the north I used to fish within 1km of shore and still get limits.

One thing that I did find is that, for me at least, spoons did not work as well out there as they do in Long Point Bay and further west. I may have been trolling too slow for them to be effective. Body baits worked well, but when the sledding got tough, the go to was worm harnesses 2mph or slower behind dipsys, riggers, whatever got them down to the fish. [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) has a lot of experience out there, no one better to get pointer from for that area.

Arranged to meet up with [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) at FishMasters around noon- outside of roadwork (still) in Delhi, was a nice 2 1/2 hr drive down #3 . After greetings, handshakes and a couple of 6-8 coasters passing hands, we launched and I followed down the Grand and out to open water. Set up over 82fow with Dipsys and RRFs. Managed 2/3 in first 25 mins and got cocky- released both. Trolled 80-90 fow catching 4 more by time [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) and his fishing partner pulled up alongside to have a good chat before they headed in. Stuck it out to 4:30 when the rain started- pulled the pin having hooked 3 more. Dipsy leads on 1 were 86-130' (most fish at 102'), speeds 2.2- 2.9 (last 3 fish at higher speeds). Wonderbread glow RRF got 1st, Nascar RRF went 1/2 losing a goodun but caught 2 in 4th qrtr and wormburners (wonderbread & blueberry muffin) did the rest. Have found Maitland a tough nut to crack with big range of depths and the fish can be anywhere in the column. Big thanks to [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) for the introduction to FishMasters (1st time)👍👍, providing the need-to-know and the guided escort 🍻👊 Took a while but 10th trip was a charm- 9 fish and great conditions... best yet!

It was great to meet you in person Jamie 👍 Thx for the 68 decos they will be on boat and trailor soon enough. Was happy to give some tips and kinda show you around. 😃..Conditions were fantastic light overcast and light breeze made for a good day to be out ..dont get many like that out there. We boxed a 2 man limit and let 2 smalls go. No double digit yet for me this season but there still some time tho the window is closing. anyway once again glad to meet you. You're a class act and thx again for the decals 🍻🎣

> Hey [@SkinnyTiller](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/10003/), how did you like the missile launcher...I mean boat ramp? I used to live just down the road overlooking Mohawk Island, but only launched at Fishmasters 1X. Great place, nice setup for mooring, but the ramp is out of this world, at least used to be. It was so steep that the door of the truck would not stay open I had fight my way out of the truck. Had a bugger of time getting the boat back on the trailer correctly as well.
> 
> 
> It is a nice area to fish, lots of bottom contour and deep and shallow shoals. You can catch a limit in 100fow or 20fow if you want. I liked it for that reason, it allows me to expand my bag of tricks. If the wind is bad from the north I used to fish within 1km of shore and still get limits.
> 
> 
> One thing that I did find is that, for me at least, spoons did not work as well out there as they do in Long Point Bay and further west. I may have been trolling too slow for them to be effective. Body baits worked well, but when the sledding got tough, the go to was worm harnesses 2mph or slower behind dipsys, riggers, whatever got them down to the fish. [@gilfisher](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5566/) has a lot of experience out there, no one better to get pointer from for that area.

While FishMasters is the steepest ramp I've launched from [@done working](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/6382/), it wasn't too crazy given NEM in Bruce has a 'bit of slope' to it too. Made the mistake when I did dunk the tiller of backing down too far- had to 're-install' the license plate on the trailer before heading home 😆 I did really like the big staging area for set-up and breakdown and the honor system for paying took me back to first few yrs on Erie launching from The Docks in Bruce. Like you said, great set-up and I'm used to a river run before open water. Only hiccup was my truck navigation kept telling me to turn onto the next street to the N! 😂 On previous trips out of Maitland my best fish have come on Bandits and Gibbs w a worm, yesterday the few spoons I ran off cheaters stunk but the RRF with a worm and wormburners did yeoman's work. I don't mind a fishery that can pull you out of the normal routine and  
 humble you too- having great fellow members provide some cheat code definitley makes the learning curve much steeper than the FishMasters ramp!

Ran am and pm charters and both did very well. Lake was well behaved so we ran out to 65 FOW and set up. Everything we presented fired. Did not use leadcore this time. markdown:
Title: Fishing Report - PT. BRUCE- Should Have Brought An Abacus

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/pt-bruce-should-have-brought-an-abacus.98023/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/pt-bruce-should-have-brought-an-abacus.98023/

Markdown Content:
[![Image 1: SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/pt-bruce-should-have-brought-an-abacus.98023/post-342893)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/pt-bruce-should-have-brought-an-abacus.98023/post-342893)

Wasn't thinking of fishing, until reading this morning's posts- kept an eye on the buoy until it got closer to the forecast by noon then got tbe ball rolling. [@King Joe](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/7142/) made it to Bruce in ~1hr on short notice and with the tiller launched and waiting, we were off 'bout 2:30. Didn't make it to the lighthouse before running into another 6-8er- [@Bouk49ers](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/5676/) coming back in with a grin on his face. Quick hello and exchange of info and we were off SW into tight 2' chop out of the WSW.

Set up over 46fow ~3 and had just set 2nd rod when 1st fired. Trolled out to 60fow, did a big loop then headed N back into 48fow where bite slowed so 180ed on course and headed downhill until we had our limits, or so we thought 🙄. Ran 4 Dipsys w leads 71-94' on 3 and 72-104' on 1, speeds 2.3-2.9. Lost 4, incl. a Bow (hooked on a P10!) and nice 'eye, and boated 13- best action 48-55fow. Wormburners in Wonderbread and green-back Blueberry Muffin did well (incl. best fish) w Nascar/Duracell RRF and Gibbs chipping in tho Nascar lost as many as it caught. Lake and wind settled nicely, then our ankles took a beating from those blasted flies. Packed it in at 7 with our 'last fish' and were last boat to trailer. Dumped the fish for a pic, and there were only 11! 🤨😂 All good as Joe took a limit home and I've only 5 to clean. Turned out to be a great day, fishing and weatherwise for trip #48. Also great to team up with [@King Joe](https://longpoint.on.ca/members/7142/) after crossing paths at the London Fishing Expo, and send him home with a few 'shingles' for the freezer 😉😁👍

title: Sept 11 outer LPB
markdown:
Title: Sept 11 outer LPB

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/sept-11-outer-lpb.98015/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/sept-11-outer-lpb.98015/

Markdown Content:
*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/sept-11-outer-lpb.98015/post-342843)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/sept-11-outer-lpb.98015/post-342843)

Headed out of Port D a little after 6:00. Fished mostly the 40-50ft depth range with just one trip out 80fow. Tried to avoid the pack which looked to be mostly in the 80-100+ range. Didn't have to deal with many boats except the ones blowing past to deeper water.

Pretty steady action from 6:30 to about 10:00 with a a fish every 5-10 min or so and a few double headers. Around 10:00 the bite slowed down when I trolled out to 80fow, the waves calmed a bit and the sun was high and bright. At about 11:30 I was back in the shallower water and slowed down to 1.8mph with green and orange harnesses behind a #1 dipsy on 2.5 setting back 125 back, fishing the bottom 10ft of water. Pretty steady fishing until I pulled lines at 2:30.

I kept my self imposed limit of 5, one shy of legal so that I can keep fishing and just in case I get badly hooked fish. The biggest one in the photo is 27", a little bigger than I like to keep. Had one bigger, but she was set back.

Toward the end, when I was using up the last worm, I sent out a metallic perch hotlips 175ft. It was the last bait in the water and I had sped up to 2.5mph after reeling the last fish on the harness. Cranking fast to bring the hotlips in felt a bump on the line, thought WTH was that, then another hit and line peeled out for several runs. At the speed that the lure had been moving, 2.5mph plus whatever speed I was cranking, I figured that it must be a rainbow. Nope, a giant 28" drum that must have been channeling its inner blue marlin. Still fun on a ML rod and 15lb braid.

Marked fish high and marked fish down low. Fished baits high and fished them low.. took 2 off goldminers with 2oz snap running 150ft of line, near useless in my opinion.   
 Took a couple small fish(smallest of the day) off riggers with DW spoon.  
 Running a harness near bottom off riggers and big DW divers was tough to improve on. [![Image 1: 20260929_203535.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72828-1728a73431da94399e1a6e880c04729b.jpg?hash=0EoT1HosrE)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20260929_203535-webp.127420/)  
 70-110fow.  
 Lots of 3-4" smelt popping out of the catch from down deep.   
 Elbow=fish,anlger/boats and miles of nets.. keep an eye.

Its not like fishing in july-August when you can pull any bait off of any presentation at any speed over any piece of water and catch fish aimlessly but there are still plenty of fish to be had if your willing and able.

Weather/conditions was mint!!   
 Beautiful day to be on the bay.

>

Old habits are hard to break.

Read and hear about people dragging their lures below fish all the time.

Having a graph and actually acting on what it shows you, whether you can believe it or not can make or break the day.

Well done. 😁🌻

I was out of Maitland Monday at 7am with a buddy. Went out 210° to 90FOW, fish were everywhere in the column. Got our 12 in 2.5 hours using RRF's & worm harnesses. All under 4lbs but still good fish. Next day another buddy came down and we went out 7am & headed to the same area. We could only take 6 fish since I still had 6 at the trailer from the day before. Decided to just use 2 rods so we could make the trip worthwhile. Fish were stacked everywhere again but not as many takers. RRF's took a couple then switched to worm harnesses which seemed to be preferred. Out to 105 FOW then turned back. Brought home 6 fish, one just over 5lbs, the rest smaller. Released 4, lost at least 4 near the boat and had one big fish that snapped the snubber (this is a first & I just changed them out 2 years ago). Waves were a little bigger from the NNE but nothing crazy. Can't believe the number of fish out there.   
 This was my 4th time out with the new Minn Kota auto-pilot, can't get over how much more enjoyable it is to be out and not have to be at the helm. What a game changer.

Took the missus out to the Elbow for the first time, ever. Not her cup of tea, but since the perch aren't around, she decided to give it a go as long as she could sleep in. Started setting lines in 80 fow again and worked our way out to 105 near the black well pipe. Riggers down 80' and 90' with worm harnesses and spoons on cheaters. Dipsys set on 3, back 90' and 120', with RRF and Bomber Long A. We caught our limit, threw some back and lost a couple at the boat due to tangles. I fried up the cheeks in butter and lemon pepper for a fresh afternoon snack. Hopefully the weather cooperates for the next few weeks to get back out there again. Or schools of perch and crappie start to arrive before hunting and trapping is in full swing.[![Image 1: PXL_20260912_185230540.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72599-bd39a1fb95b638970ec6def4c328905a.jpg?hash=CjSKxiU2wU)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/pxl_20260912_185230540-webp.126987/)

*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/the-elbow-monday-sept-7th.98002/post-342722)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/the-elbow-monday-sept-7th.98002/post-342722)

Headed East about 6:15 am, bumpier than we thought it would be on the way out.. Reached 80 fow and dropped lines. With 4 rods in the water, the fish came fast and furious. 2 dipsys set on 3, back 90' and 120'. Riggers with balls down 60' and 70', both with cheaters. Bandit, Bomber Long A, Ripplin red fin, worm harness, greasy chicken spoon and blue berry muffin spoon all firing. Culled some smaller fish and had to release 3 as we reeled in the set. Back at the marina by 9:30. Landed a monster on the way out as well.[![Image 1: PXL_20260907_142206006.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72495-6621d7655626b19e7c1ae33e4fc449ed.jpg?hash=tLHbnpPAPY)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/pxl_20260907_142206006-webp.126803/)[![Image 2: PXL_20260907_151540450.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/72/72494-32740f2e88735507ccb0463c37474d9a.jpg?hash=bgUv878pyt)](https://longpoint.on.ca/attachments/pxl_20260907_151540450-webp.126802/)

markdown:
Title: Yak Attack, Sept 16 afternoon/eve Port Bruce

URL Source: http://longpoint.on.ca/threads/yak-attack-sept-16-afternoon-eve-port-bruce.98036/

Final URL: https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/yak-attack-sept-16-afternoon-eve-port-bruce.98036/

Markdown Content:
*   [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/yak-attack-sept-16-afternoon-eve-port-bruce.98036/post-342959)

*   [#1](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/yak-attack-sept-16-afternoon-eve-port-bruce.98036/post-342959)

Big thanks to those the responded to my "Eyes on Pt. Bruce" to add clarity on wind/waves off Port Bruce. Beach launches can add another level of challenge with waves, if any. As it was, when I showed to Bruce beach, slight rollers only. No issue launching at around 2:30 pm.

As the plan, was going to focus on shallows. In effect, back to my early roots of yak fishing Erie (and before the pedal drive). Shallow (30' ish) and parrallel to shore. Add to the 'back to roots'....Bruce and Burwell are where I cut my teeth years (over 10 now) yak attacking. Burwell...now screwed due to the upstream launch dude ripping up the sub launch area....and Bruce, due to beach erosion, now with huge steep beech sand dunes. Was great to be back to Bruce...and thanks to Skinny Tiller who lit that fire again for me, here. Anyway, to the report....

Cruised to 35' and set bananas (2 and 3) with harnesses. Pink panties on 2, Greasy Chicken Wing on 3. The screen was FULL, top to bottom. Within minutes, I'm on...and loose my first off #2. 5 or so minutes later...a chunky walleye comes to net off 2. I cruise to 36-37, trying to get a less busy screen (thinking that is a mixed bag of fish causing that screen)....then turn to cruise parrallel west- southwest. Frequent fish on and lands...a range of species. The odd walleye thrown in.

Far west of Bruce, and in a dry spell including a bare screen, I turn SE and head a bit deeper running to 42' before coming back around and coming back shallow (36'), now east of Bruce. While out, I see a big pontoon boat that had been sitting my whole time thus far. I thought they were bottom bouncing/jigging...and they were but...they were broken down. I offered to pull em in..>HAH....but they said they had someone coming. Poor dudes. They were there a LONG time before somebody came.

Through my time, NUMEROUS fish caught, a handful lost before I make the short...the blessedly short run (compared to my now-usual Erieau DEEP runs) home. In total, landed 8 walleye, lost 3... 5 white perch and 2 sheeps. While I went with 24 worms, I was rationing near the end....hah. MOST action, save 1 walleye, were from the 35-36'. Mix between Greasy Chicken and Nascar (pink panties got retired earlier). Was back at the beach by 7:00 loaded and leaving.

Thanks for chatting on the water Skinny Tiller.
